#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Codingame puzzle: 
https://www.codingame.com/ide/puzzle/
"""

#region Boilerplate

from __future__ import annotations

# ruff: noqa: E402


import math # noqa: F401
import sys
from itertools import combinations as _combinations # noqa: F401
from types import NotImplementedType # noqa: F401
from typing import ( # noqa: F401
    Any,
    ClassVar,
    Final,
    Generator,      
    Generic,
    Iterable,
    Iterator,
    NamedTuple,
    Optional,
    Protocol,
    runtime_checkable,
    TypeAlias,
    TypeVar,
    cast,
    overload,
)

from enum import Enum, auto, IntEnum # noqa: F401

from functools import total_ordering # noqa: F401
from queue import PriorityQueue # noqa: F401

class NoValue:
    pass

NO_VALUE = NoValue()

if sys.version_info >= (3, 12):
    from typing import Self, override
else:
    # pyright: ignore[reportUnreachable]
    try:
        from typing_extensions import Self, override  # type: ignore[import]
    except ImportError:
        Self: TypeAlias = Any
        def override(func: Any) -> Any:
            return func


STANDALONE = False
if len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == "--standalone":
    STANDALONE = True
    sys.argv = [ sys.argv[0] ] + sys.argv[2:]

DEBUG = True
DEBUG_INPUT = True

def dp(*args, debug: Optional[bool]=None, **kwargs):
    if debug is None:
        debug = DEBUG
    if debug:
        print(*args, **kwargs, file=sys.stderr)

def dpinput() -> str:
    result = input()
    dp(result, debug=DEBUG_INPUT)
    return result

#----------------------------------------------------------
#endregion

#region Problem Statement
"""
Simple Makefile Processor
=========================

Parse a simplified makefile and output, in order, all actions required to
build the specified target(s).

INPUT FORMAT
------------
Line 1:  n_files — integer, number of preexisting files
Lines 2…: one "fileName fileTime" pair per line (n_files lines; timestamps ignored for now)
Next:    space-separated target names to build (blank line = use default target)
Next:    n_lines — integer, number of makefile lines that follow
Lines …: The makefile content (exactly n_lines lines)

MAKEFILE FORMAT
---------------
A rule names a target and its prerequisites, followed by zero or more
action lines:

    target: dep1 dep2 ...
    <TAB>command token1 token2 ...
    <TAB>command token1 token2 ...

  - Rule line: any non-blank, non-tab line containing ':'. Everything
    before ':' is one or more whitespace-separated target names; everything
    after is whitespace-separated prerequisites.
  - Action line: begins with a single TAB character. Belongs to the most
    recently defined rule.
  - Comment: '#' begins a comment that extends to end of line. May appear
    on any line type. Stripped before parsing.
  - Blank lines: ignored.

SIMPLIFIED CONSTRAINTS (the puzzle removes real-make complexity)
----------------------------------------------------------------
  1. No variable/macro definitions (CC = gcc etc. do not appear).
  2. Only three built-in macros are supported; each appears as a complete,
     standalone token — no concatenation with surrounding text:
       $@  current target name
       $<  first prerequisite
       $^  all prerequisites, space-separated, in definition order
  3. No dot-directives (.PHONY, .SUFFIXES, …).
  4. No static pattern rules (e.g. `%.o: %.c`). A rule line may, however,
     list multiple plain targets before the colon:
       foo bar: baz
     This is exactly equivalent to two separate rules, one for each target,
     sharing the same prerequisites and action lines. Built-in macros such
     as $@ expand relative to each individual target. The first target named
     on the first rule line of the makefile is the default target.
  5. No filename wildcards or path canonicalization; targets are compared
     as plain strings.
  6. Timestamps are ignored. A target that has at least one action is
     always considered out-of-date and must be rebuilt.
  7. A target that has no rule at all is assumed to already exist (like an
     up-to-date source file); it needs no actions and has no prerequisites.
  8. All tokens are simple whitespace-delimited strings; ':' and '#' never
     appear inside a token. '$' only begins one of the three built-in macros.
  9. Action lines are the only lines that begin with a TAB; TABs do not
     appear elsewhere.
 10. A target name may appear in multiple rule lines (whether through the
     multi-target shorthand or as separate rules). Its prerequisites are the
     union of all definitions, and its actions are the concatenation of all
     definition action lines in order of appearance.

BUILD SEMANTICS
---------------
  1. If n_targets == 0, build the first target defined in the makefile
     (the "default" target — the one that appears first as a rule LHS).
  2. Each target is built at most once per invocation.
  3. All prerequisites of a target are fully built before the target itself.
  4. When build order is not constrained by the dependency graph, targets
     with lexicographically smaller names are built first.
  5. Actions are only emitted for a target that has at least one action line.
  6. Before building, the entire dependency graph is checked for cycles. If
     any cycle exists (even among targets not being built), the build is
     aborted immediately.

OUTPUT FORMAT
-------------
  - For every action that must be executed, output it on its own line:
    tokens separated by a single space, no leading or trailing whitespace,
    with built-in macros already expanded.
  - After all actions, output exactly:  [Build complete]
  - If the dependency graph contains a cycle, output exactly:
      [Circular dependencies detected]
    No actions are emitted and [Build complete] is suppressed.

EXAMPLE
-------
Input (Text iside <> is appropriately replaced by actual input; blank lines are shown explicitly):
    0
    <blank-line>
    7
    all: main.o util.o
    <TAB>gcc -o $@ $^
    main.o: main.c
    <TAB>gcc -c $< -o $@
    util.o: util.c
    <TAB>gcc -c $< -o $@

Output:
    gcc -c main.c -o main.o
    gcc -c util.c -o util.o
    gcc -o all main.o util.o
    [Build complete]

Explanation: default target is 'all'; its prerequisites ['main.o', 'util.o']
are sorted lexicographically so main.o is built first, then util.o, then all.
main.c and util.c have no rule so they are assumed to exist already.
"""
#endregion

Token = str
TargetName = str

class LineType(Enum):
    RULE = auto()
    ACTION = auto()
    BLANK = auto()

class MakefileError(Exception):
    """Raised when the makefile is invalid or cannot be processed."""
    
    def __init__(self, message: str, line_no: Optional[int] = None, line_text: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
        if line_no is not None:
            message = f"Makefile line {line_no}: {message}"
        if line_text is not None:
            message = f"{message}:  {line_text!r}"
        super().__init__(message)

class MakefileLineError(MakefileError):
    """Raised when a specific line of the makefile is invalid."""
    def __init__(self, line: MakefileLine, message: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(message, line_no=line.line_no, line_text=line.raw_line)

class MakefileCycleError(MakefileError):
    """Raised when a circular dependency is detected in the makefile."""
    def __init__(self, target_name: TargetName) -> None:
        super().__init__(f"Circular dependency detected while building {target_name!r}")
        
class MakefileLine:
    """A parsed line of the makefile, with tokens and metadata."""
    
    line_no: int
    """1-based line number in the original makefile."""

    raw_line: str
    """Original line text, with comments and whitespace intact."""
    
    comment: str | None = None
    """Comment text, including the leading '#', or None if no comment."""
    
    is_action: bool = False
    """True if this line is an action line (begins with a TAB)."""
    
    stripped: str
    """Line text with comments and leading/trailing whitespace removed."""
    
    is_rule: bool = False
    """True if this line is a rule line (non-blank, non-action line containing ':')."""
    
    target_tokens: list[Token]
    """Tokens from the rule's target part (before ':'). Empty if not a rule."""
    
    tokens: list[Token]
    """For actions, tokens from the action line. For rules, tokens from the dependencies. Empy for blank lines."""
    
    @property
    def is_blank(self) -> bool:
        """True if this line is blank (only whitespace and/or a comment)."""
        return not self.is_action and not self.is_rule
    
    def __init__(self, line_no: int, raw_line: str) -> None:
        self.line_no = line_no
        self.raw_line = raw_line
        line = raw_line.rstrip()
        i_comment = line.find('#')
        if i_comment >= 0:
            self.comment = line[i_comment:]
            line = line[:i_comment].rstrip()
        if line.startswith('\t'):
            self.is_action = True
            line = line[1:]
        line = line.strip()
        self.stripped = line
        self.target_tokens = []
        if not self.is_action:
            i_colon = line.find(':')
            if i_colon >= 0:
                if '$' in line:
                    raise MakefileLineError(self, "Rule lines cannot contain macro expansions")
                self.is_rule = True
                target_str = line[:i_colon].strip()
                if len(target_str) == 0:
                    raise MakefileLineError(self, "Invalid rule line with empty target")
                self.target_tokens = target_str.split()
                line = line[i_colon + 1:].strip()
        
        self.tokens = line.split() if line else []
        
class Action(NamedTuple):
    """A single action line, with its tokens and reference to the rule it belongs to."""
    original_tokens: list[Token]
    """Tokens without macros expanded"""
    
    tokens: list[Token]
    """Tokens with macros expanded"""
    
    line: MakefileLine
    """The original MakefileLine that defined this action, used for error reporting."""
    
    rule: Rule
    """The Rule that this action belongs to, used for macro expansion."""
    
    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return ' '.join(self.tokens)
    
    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Action(tokens={self.tokens!r}, line_no={self.line.line_no})"

class Rule(NamedTuple):
    """A single rule line with a single target, its dependencies, and actions.
       If a rule line contains multiple targets, a separate Rule and Actions will be created for each.
    """
    target: TargetName
    deps: list[TargetName]
    actions: list[Action]
    line: MakefileLine
    
    def expand_tokens(self, tokens: Iterable[Token]) -> list[Token]:
        """Expand built-in macros in the given action tokens using this rule's target and deps."""
        result: list[Token] = []
        for tok in tokens:
            if tok.startswith('$'):
                if tok == '$@':
                    result.append(self.target)
                elif tok == '$<':
                    if self.deps:
                        result.append(self.deps[0])
                elif tok == '$^':
                    result.extend(self.deps)
                else:
                    raise MakefileLineError(self.line, f"Unknown macro {tok!r} in action")
            else:
                result.append(tok)
        return result
    
    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.target}: {' '.join(self.deps)}\n" + '\n'.join(f"\t{action}" for action in self.actions)
    
    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Rule(target={self.target!r}, deps={self.deps!r}, actions={self.actions!r}, line_no={self.line.line_no})"

class Target(NamedTuple):
    """A single named target, with its rules, dependencies, and actions."""
    name: TargetName
    rules: list[Rule]
    deps: set[TargetName]
    
    def iter_actions(self) -> Generator[Action, None, None]:
        """Iterate over all actions for this target, in order of appearance in the makefile."""
        for rule in self.rules:
            for action in rule.actions:
                yield action
    
    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"Target({self.name!r})"
    
    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"Target(name={self.name!r}, rules={self.rules!r}, deps={sorted(self.deps)!r}, actions={list(self.iter_actions())!r})"
        
    
class Makefile:
    lines: list[MakefileLine]
    targets: dict[TargetName, Target]
    default_target: Target | None = None
    
    def get_target(self, name: TargetName) -> Target:
        """Get the Target object for the given name, creating it if necessary."""
        target = self.targets.get(name)
        if target is None:
            target = Target(name=name, rules=[], deps=set())
            self.targets[name] = target
        return target
    
    def __init__(self, lines: Iterable[str]) -> None:
        self.lines = [MakefileLine(i + 1, line) for i, line in enumerate(lines)]
        self.targets = {}
        current_rules: list[Rule] = []
        """The rules currently being defined.  Empty when not processing a rule. May have > 1 rule when processing a rule line with multiple targets."""

        for line in self.lines:
            if line.is_action:
                if len(current_rules) == 0:
                    raise MakefileLineError(line, "Action line without preceding rule line")
                else:
                    for current_rule in current_rules:
                        action = Action(line.tokens, current_rule.expand_tokens(line.tokens), line, current_rule)
                        current_rule.actions.append(action)
            elif line.is_rule:
                targets = [ self.get_target(name) for name in line.target_tokens ]
                if len(targets) == 0:
                    raise MakefileLineError(line, "Rule line with no targets")
                if self.default_target is None:
                    self.default_target = targets[0]
                deps = line.tokens
                current_rules = []
                for target in targets:
                    current_rule = Rule(target.name, deps, [], line)
                    current_rules.append(current_rule)
                    target.rules.append(current_rule)
                    for dep in deps:
                        target.deps.add(dep)
                        
    def find_cycles(self) -> list[TargetName]:
        """Detect if there are any cycles in the dependency graph. Returns a list of target names involved in a cycle, or an empty list if no cycles."""
        visited: set[TargetName] = set()
        stack: set[TargetName] = set()
        cycles: set[TargetName] = set()

        def visit(target_name: TargetName) -> None:
            if target_name in visited:
                return
            if target_name in stack:
                cycles.add(target_name)
                return
            stack.add(target_name)
            target = self.get_target(target_name)
            for dep in target.deps:
                visit(dep)
            stack.remove(target_name)
            visited.add(target_name)

        for target_name in list(self.targets.keys()):
            visit(target_name)

        return sorted(cycles)
                    
    def build(
        self,
        requested_targets: Optional[list[TargetName]] = None,
        file_times: Optional[dict[TargetName, int]] = None,
    ) -> Iterable[Action]:
        """Build the specified targets (or the default target if None), generating the sequence of actions to execute."""
        if requested_targets is None:
            if self.default_target is None:
                return
            requested_targets = [self.default_target.name]

        # Mutable copy — updated as targets are built
        times: dict[TargetName, int] = dict(file_times) if file_times else {}
        # Each newly-built target gets a strictly increasing timestamp higher than any existing one
        build_clock = [max(times.values(), default=-1) + 1]

        processed: set[TargetName] = set()

        def is_out_of_date(target_name: TargetName) -> bool:
            target_time = times.get(target_name)
            if target_time is None:
                return True  # doesn't exist
            target = self.get_target(target_name)
            if not target.rules:
                return False  # pure source file, never out of date
            all_deps = target.deps
            if not all_deps:
                return False  # exists with no prerequisites → up to date
            for dep in all_deps:
                dep_time = times.get(dep)
                if dep_time is None or dep_time >= target_time:
                    return True
            return False

        def build_one(target_name: TargetName) -> Iterable[Action]:
            if target_name in processed:
                return
            processed.add(target_name)
            target = self.get_target(target_name)

            # Ensure prerequisites are up to date first (may update their timestamps)
            for dep in sorted(target.deps):
                yield from build_one(dep)

            if is_out_of_date(target_name):
                dp(f"Building target: {target_name!r}")
                for action in target.iter_actions():
                    yield action
                times[target_name] = build_clock[0]
                build_clock[0] += 1
            else:
                dp(f"Target {target_name!r} is up to date, skipping")

        for target_name in sorted(requested_targets):
            yield from build_one(target_name)

    def build_to_stdout(
        self,
        requested_targets: Optional[list[TargetName]] = None,
        file_times: Optional[dict[TargetName, int]] = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Build the specified targets (or the default target if None), printing actions to stdout."""
        for action in self.build(requested_targets, file_times=file_times):
            print(action)
        print("[Build complete]")
        
    def dumps(self) -> str:
        """Return a string representation of the makefile for debugging."""
        
        result = []
        for target in sorted(self.targets.values(), key=lambda t: t.name):
            result.append(repr(target))
        return '\n'.join(result)


def main() -> None:
    n_files = int(dpinput())
    file_times: dict[str, int] = {}
    for _ in range(n_files):
        parts = dpinput().split()
        file_times[parts[0]] = int(parts[1])

    target_names_line = dpinput().strip()
    target_names = target_names_line.split() if target_names_line else []
    requested = target_names if target_names else None

    n_lines = int(dpinput())
    makefile_lines = [dpinput() for _ in range(n_lines)]
    makefile = Makefile(makefile_lines)

    cycles = makefile.find_cycles()
    if cycles:
        dp(f"Circular dependencies detected in targets: {cycles}")
        print("[Circular dependencies detected]")
        return

    dp("Building...")
    makefile.build_to_stdout(requested, file_times=file_times)
    
if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
data.statement:
A <<Makefile>> is a build script that describes dependencies between dated <<files>>, and the <<actions>> required to build a <<target file>> from its <<prerequisite files>> if it is outdated or missing; <<actions>> are executed in an order such that every <<prerequisite>> is up to date before it is needed.

Your task is to implement a simplified <<make>> utility: read a list of [[preexistingFile]]s with associated [[fileTime]]s, a list of <<targets>> to build, and a Makefile, then print the actions that would be executed, in order.

<<Makefile syntax>>

A <<Makefile>> is a sequence of <<rules>> and <<actions>>, with optional <<comments>>.

<<Comments>>
A {{#}} character begins a comment that extends to the end of the line. Comments are removed before applying other parsing rules.

<<Whitespace>>
After using {{TAB}} to identify <<actions>> (see below), leading and trailing whitespace are ignored, as are blank lines and extra spaces not needed to separate tokens.

<<Rules>>

A <<rule>> associates <<targets>> with <<prerequisites>>. Each of these is generally a <<file>>, but can be any valid token string:

`
target1 [target2 ...] : [prereq1 ...]
`

To the left of the {{:}} is a whitespace-separated list of one or more <<targets>>. To the right is a whitespace-separated list of zero or more <<prerequisites>>. Whitespace adjacent to the {{:}} is optional. If multiple targets appear before the {{:}}, it is equivalent to writing a separate identical rule for each target.

A <<target>> may appear in more than one <<rule>>. Its prerequisites are the <<union>> of prerequisites in all its rules, and its <<actions>> are the <<concatenation>> of all associated rule actions, in order of appearance.

<<Actions>>

An <<action>> is any line that begins with a {{TAB}}. It is associated with the preceding <<rule>>. Applying the whitespace rules above yields a sequence of tokens. Any token that matches a built-in <<macro>> (see below) is replaced by its expansion. When the <<action>> is executed, the resulting tokens are printed as a single line of output with single-space delimiters.

<<Built-in macros>>

Within an <<action>>, built-in <<macros>> may appear as whole tokens. They are replaced by their expansions before the line is printed:

```
| Macro | Expands to
|-------|-----------
| $@    | The target being built
| $<    | The first prerequisite of the associated rule
| $^    | All prerequisites of the rule, space-separated,
|       |   in rule definition order
```

<<Build semantics>>

- If a file exists prior to the build, it has an integer [[fileTime]]. The higher the [[fileTime]], the more recently the file was last updated.
- A non-preexisting target, or a preexisting target that is as old or older than any of its prerequisites, is out of date.
- A preexisting file with no prerequisites is up to date.
- Building a target effectively updates its [[fileTime]] and makes any target for which it is a prerequisite out of date.
- Before a target is built, all of its prerequisites must be fully up to date.
- If no <<required targets>> are explicitly given in [[cmdArgs]], the first <<target>> in the first <<rule>> of the Makefile is used.
- Targets that are not needed to bring the <<required targets>> up to date are not built.
- When two targets can otherwise be built in any order, the one whose filename is lexicographically smaller is built first.
- Each target is built at most once.
- A target that has no <<actions>> produces no output, but its prerequisites are still built.
- If a dependency cycle exists anywhere in the Makefile--even among targets not being built--the build is aborted prior to executing any action.

<<Example>>

The following Makefile compiles two source files into object files, then links them into a program.

```
all: util.o main.o
	gcc -o $@ $^
util.o: util.c
	gcc -c $< -o $@
main.o: main.c
	gcc -c $< -o $@
```

Assume [[cmdArgs]] is empty, so the default target <<all>> is built. Assuming <<main.c>> and <<util.c>> are the only preexisting files, the build proceeds as follows: <<util.o>> and <<main.o>> are prerequisites of <<all>> and must be built first. Between <<util.o>> and <<main.o>>, neither depends on the other, so the lexicographically smaller name <<main.o>> is built first.

The actions output are:

```
gcc -c main.c -o main.o
gcc -c util.c -o util.o
gcc -o all util.o main.o
[Build complete]
```

Note that {{$^}} in the <<all>> rule expands to <<util.o main.o>>—-the prerequisites in their given <<rule>> order, not the order they were built.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

A Makefile is a build script that describes dependencies between dated files, and the actions required to build a target file from its prerequisite files if it is outdated or missing; actions are executed in an order such that every prerequisite is up to date before it is needed.

Your task is to implement a simplified make utility: read a list of preexistingFiles with associated fileTimes, a list of targets to build, and a Makefile, then print the actions that would be executed, in order.

Makefile syntax

A Makefile is a sequence of rules and actions, with optional comments.

Comments
A # character begins a comment that extends to the end of the line. Comments are removed before applying other parsing rules.

Whitespace
After using TAB to identify actions (see below), leading and trailing whitespace are ignored, as are blank lines and extra spaces not needed to separate tokens.

Rules

A rule associates targets with prerequisites. Each of these is generally a file, but can be any valid token string:


target1 [target2 ...] : [prereq1 ...]


To the left of the : is a whitespace-separated list of one or more targets. To the right is a whitespace-separated list of zero or more prerequisites. Whitespace adjacent to the : is optional. If multiple targets appear before the :, it is equivalent to writing a separate identical rule for each target.

A target may appear in more than one rule. Its prerequisites are the union of prerequisites in all its rules, and its actions are the concatenation of all associated rule actions, in order of appearance.

Actions

An action is any line that begins with a TAB. It is associated with the preceding rule. Applying the whitespace rules above yields a sequence of tokens. Any token that matches a built-in macro (see below) is replaced by its expansion. When the action is executed, the resulting tokens are printed as a single line of output with single-space delimiters.

Built-in macros

Within an action, built-in macros may appear as whole tokens. They are replaced by their expansions before the line is printed:


| Macro | Expands to
|-------|-----------
| $@    | The target being built
| $<    | The first prerequisite of the associated rule
| $^    | All prerequisites of the rule, space-separated,
|       |   in rule definition order


Build semantics

- If a file exists prior to the build, it has an integer fileTime. The higher the fileTime, the more recently the file was last updated.
- A non-preexisting target, or a preexisting target that is as old or older than any of its prerequisites, is out of date.
- A preexisting file with no prerequisites is up to date.
- Building a target effectively updates its fileTime and makes any target for which it is a prerequisite out of date.
- Before a target is built, all of its prerequisites must be fully up to date.
- If no required targets are explicitly given in cmdArgs, the first target in the first rule of the Makefile is used.
- Targets that are not needed to bring the required targets up to date are not built.
- When two targets can otherwise be built in any order, the one whose filename is lexicographically smaller is built first.
- Each target is built at most once.
- A target that has no actions produces no output, but its prerequisites are still built.
- If a dependency cycle exists anywhere in the Makefile--even among targets not being built--the build is aborted prior to executing any action.

Example

The following Makefile compiles two source files into object files, then links them into a program.


all: util.o main.o
	gcc -o $@ $^
util.o: util.c
	gcc -c $< -o $@
main.o: main.c
	gcc -c $< -o $@


Assume cmdArgs is empty, so the default target all is built. Assuming main.c and util.c are the only preexisting files, the build proceeds as follows: util.o and main.o are prerequisites of all and must be built first. Between util.o and main.o, neither depends on the other, so the lexicographically smaller name main.o is built first.

The actions output are:


gcc -c main.c -o main.o
gcc -c util.c -o util.o
gcc -o all util.o main.o
[Build complete]


Note that $^ in the all rule expands to util.o main.o—-the prerequisites in their given rule order, not the order they were built.




   

      
Input

      
Line 1: An integer nFiles, the number of preexisting files.
Next nFiles lines: A preexistingFile and its integer timestamp fileTime, one file per line.
Next Line: The commandline arguments cmdArgs, consisting of space-delimited required targets to build, or an empty line.
Next Line: An integer nLines, the number of lines in the Makefile.
Next nLines lines: The contents of the Makefile, one makefileLine at a time.

   

   

      
Output

      
If a circular dependency is detected:
    A single line: 
      [Circular dependencies detected]

If a circular dependency is not detected:
    One line per action executed:> The tokens of the action, separated by single spaces,
        with all built-in macros already expanded. Actions are printed in the order they are executed.
    Final line:
      [Build complete]

   

   

      
Constraints

      
0 <= nFiles <= 20
1 <= length(preexistingFile) <= 100
0 <= fileTime <= 1000
0 <= length(cmdArgs) <= 100
1 <= nLines <= 100
0 <= length(makefileLine) <= 100

preexistingFile consists of printable ASCII characters and does not contain whitespace, $, :, or #.
All fileTime values may be assumed to be in the past.

Within the Makefile:
- At least one rule is defined.
Every file consists of 1-100 printable ASCII characters and does not contain whitespace, $, :, or #.
- Every required target either appears as a preexistingFile or is the target of at least one rule.
- Every action is preceded by at least one rule.
- TAB characters do not appear anywhere except as the first character of an action.

   

   

      
Example

      

         

            
Input

            
2
main.c 100
util.c 100

6
all: util.o main.o
	gcc -o $@ $^
util.o: util.c
	gcc -c $< -o $@
main.o: main.c
	gcc -c $< -o $@


         

         

            
Output

            
gcc -c main.c -o main.o
gcc -c util.c -o util.o
gcc -o all util.o main.o
[Build complete]
